messages:
alex.support: Heads up — multiple hosted-inference customers reporting sudden spikes of 5xxs and timeouts since ~10:12 UTC. Examples: /v1/generate -> 502 Bad Gateway, /v1/chat/completions -> 504 Gateway Timeout. Tickets: #40821, #40822. Logs show repeated "cache GET timeout" and long blocking on KV prefix reads.

sophie.custsuccess: AsterHealth + DataQ escalated to CS — Aster reports ~25% requests failing, DataQ seeing elevated latency and request churn. They want ETA.

sam.oncall: oncall here. pulling logs now. anyone see recent deploys or config changes? @deploy-bot any rollouts around 10:00-10:15?

deploy-bot: prod-deploy: model-router v2.3.1 rolled to us-east-1 at 10:09 UTC (no rollback).

jin.eng-runtime: i'm seeing a ton of redis connection errors and i/o timeouts from the prefix cache client. sample snippets below from runtime logs: 

```
ERROR cache/redis.go:134 - GET prefix:"usr:session:*": timeout after 150ms connErr="i/o timeout"
ERROR gateway/proxy.go:212 - upstream error - proxy failed to build response, err="cache read failure"
WARN runtime/batcher.go:88 - request stalled waiting for KV cache (duration=320ms)
```

maria.eng-sre: infra metrics corroborate — redis-us-east primary pods showed memory spike + evictions and file descriptor pressure. maxclients peaked near 10k which hit the connection limit. Redis latency p50 went from 2ms -> 250ms for ~10m window. memcached cluster seems healthy (no correlating errors).

alex.support: Impacted endpoints are hosted inference routes (chat/generate/embed). Customers get 502/504 from the gateway, not model errors. Are we currently treating cache failures as blocking the request instead of best-effort?

jin.eng-runtime: by default prefix/KV cache is synchronous for some hot paths to ensure consistent completions; however we have a circuit-breaker flag that can make cache best-effort. looks like CB stayed closed and the client kept waiting on slow redis. we should open the CB to bypass cache ASAP.

sam.oncall: action plan (hot):
1) open circuit-breaker to bypass prefix/KV cache for hosted API (hot config flip)
2) restart redis master pods in us-east-1 and scale replicas if needed
3) increase redis client pool + warn on maxclients in infra alerts
4) roll config tweaks to mark cache failures non-blocking in runtime
5) notify CS + affected customers with mitigation steps

maria.eng-sre: i just flipped a hot flag to set CACHE_BYPASS=true for routes /v1/* at the edge layer (10:18 UTC) so runtime will skip synchronous cache reads. also kicked a restart of statefulset/redis-us-east: `kubectl rollout restart statefulset/redis-us-east`.

cache-bot: pod/redis-master-0 restarted at 10:20 UTC; pod became Ready at 10:22 UTC and rejoined the cluster.

jin.eng-runtime: after bypassing cache, 5xx spike dropped almost immediately. metrics: 5xx rate went from ~6% -> 0.4% within 3 minutes, median request latency fell from 1.8s -> 420ms. looks like the cache blocking was the dominant failure mode.

alex.support: i've updated both customer tickets with the current mitigation and a repro for them to validate. Repro steps we sent:

```
# repro (hosted)
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"xlarge-1","input":"hello world"}'
# if you see 502/504 or a body with "cache read failure" please capture response headers and request-id
```

sophie.custsuccess: AsterHealth confirmed they see request success improving after ~10:19 UTC and appreciate the quick workaround. They asked whether this will be permanent or if we expect followups.

maria.eng-sre: temporary mitigation notes: prefix caching left disabled for hosted routes until we patch the redis client handling (suspect leak/slow pipeline when many large TTL keys are present). next steps:
- run memprof and inspect for large value sizes + TTL churn
- add backoff + rate limiter on cache writes for hot prefixes
- implement circuit-breaker unit tests in runtime repo
- increase infra alerting for redis file descriptors / maxclients threshold
- consider moving to cluster-mode sharded redis or increase replica count in us-east

sam.oncall: filed incident INC-2026-03-15-cache and added initial timeline + mitigation. assigning postmortem to eng-sre and eng-runtime.

jin.eng-runtime: quick note on reproability we captured in logs — large multi-tenant prefix keys (session blobs + user embeddings) were being written with long TTLs and a few very large values caused write amplification and increased memory churn. when eviction + maxclients triggered, clients blocked and sync reads waited. this is consistent with the i/o timeouts we saw.

alex.support: will keep tickets open until postmortem + RCA. i've left suggested customer messaging: explain transient cache outage, mitigation done (bypassed cache), and upcoming fixes (circuit-breaker, rate limiter, infra scale).

sophie.custsuccess: customers asked for ETA on permanent fix — please update once triage complete.

maria.eng-sre: ETA: hotfix (circuit-breaker + config defaults) today; broader infra changes (sharding/scale) next week. we'll post a followup in #incidents and the postmortem doc.

sam.oncall: tagging for follow-up: @jin.eng-runtime @maria.eng-sre @alex.support @sophie.custsuccess. I'll monitor for recurrence for 24h and then reconcile.

alex.support: closing thread for now — mitigation successful, customers notified, incident created. will paste postmortem link here when ready. :white_check_mark:
